'''Ayatokunaka Shrine''' (綾戸国中神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|qid=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture}}{{ill|Kyoto|en|Kyoto|qid=Q34600|lt=Kyoto City}}{{ill|Minami-ku, Kyoto|bg|Минами|ca|Minami (Kyoto)|ceb|Minami Ku (subdistrito sa Hapon, Kyōto-fu)|de|Minami-ku (Kyōto)|eo|Kvartalo Minami-ku (Kioto)|eu|Minami-ku (Kyoto)|fa|مینامی، کیوتو|fi|Minami-ku (Kioto)|fr|Minami-ku (Kyoto)|id|Minami-ku, Kyōto|it|Minami-ku (Kyoto)|ja|南区 (京都市)|ko|미나미구 (교토시)|my|မိနမိရပ်ကွက်၊ ကျိုတို|ru|Минами (Киото)|th|เขตมินามิ (เกียวโต)|tr|Minami, Kyoto|uk|Район Мінамі (Кіото)|zh|南區 (京都市)|zh_yue|南區 (京都)|qid=Q1154649|lt=Minami Ward}}. It was originally two shrines, {{ill|Ayato Shrine|ja|綾戸神社}} and {{ill|Kuninaka Shrine|ja|国中神社|qid=Q11420409}}, which were merged. The {{ill|Gion Matsuri|ar|مهرجان غيون|bcl|Gion Matsuri|de|Gion-Matsuri|es|Gion Matsuri|eu|Gion Matsuri|fa|جشن گیئون|fi|Gion-matsuri|fr|Gion matsuri|id|Gion Matsuri|it|Gion Matsuri|ja|祇園祭|ko|기온마쓰리|mai|जिओन मातसुरी|ms|Gion Matsuri|my|ဂိအွန်းပွဲတော်|ne|जिओन मातसुरी|pl|Festiwal Gion|pt|Gion Matsuri|ro|Festivalul Gion|ru|Гион-мацури|sa|जियोन महोत्सवः|simple|Gion Festival|sv|Gion Matsuri|th|เทศกาลกิอง|tr|Gion Festivali|zh|祇園祭|qid=Q979873|lt=Gion Festival}} is a ritual celebrated jointly with {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|en|Yasaka Shrine|qid=Q692714|lt=Yasaka Shrine}}.

== History ==
=== Ayato Shrine ===
It is said to have been founded in the 15th year of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|qid=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai}} ({{ill|521|ab|521|af|521|am|521 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|521|ar|521|ary|521|ast|521|avk|521|az|521|azb|۵۲۱ (میلادی)|be|521|be_x_old|521|bg|521|bn|৫২১|bpy|মারি ৫২১|br|521|bs|521.|ca|521|cdo|521 nièng|ceb|521|ckb|٥٢١|crh|521|cs|521|cv|521|cy|521|da|521|de|521|el|521|eml|521|eo|521|es|521|et|521|eu|521|fa|۵۲۱ (میلادی)|fi|521|fo|521|fr|521|fy|521|ga|521|gan|521年|gd|521|gl|521|he|521|hi|521|hr|521.|ht|521 (almanak jilyen)|hu|521|hy|521|id|521|io|521|it|521|ja|521年|jv|521|ka|521|kk|521 жыл|ko|521년|la|521|lb|521|lij|521|lmo|521|lt|521 m.|map_bms|521|mdf|521|mg|521|mhr|521|mk|521|mr|इ.स. ५२१|mrj|521 и|ms|521|mzn|۵۲۱|nah|521|nap|521|nds|521|nds_nl|521|new|सन् ५२१|nl|521|nn|521|no|521|nso|521|oc|521|or|୫୨୧|os|521-æм аз|pl|521|pnb|521|pt|521|qu|521|ro|521|ru|521 год|rue|521|sa|५२१|scn|521|sd|521ع|sh|521.|shn|521|sk|521|sl|521|sq|521|sr|521|su|521|sv|521|sw|521|tg|Соли 521|th|พ.ศ. 1064|tk|521|tl|521|tly|521|tr|521|tt|521 ел|uk|521|ur|521ء|uz|521|vec|521|vi|521|war|521|wuu|521年|xmf|521|zh|521年|zh_min_nan|521 nî|zh_yue|521年|qid=Q31436|lt=521 AD}}), and was once known as Ōi-sha, serving as the purification deity of the Ōigawa ({{ill|Katsura River|arz|نهر كاتسورا|fa|رود کاتسورا|fi|Katsurajoki|fr|Katsura-gawa|id|Sungai Katsura|it|Katsura (fiume)|ja|桂川 (淀川水系)|ko|가쓰라강|my|ခဆွတ်ရမြစ်|ru|Кацура (река)|th|แม่น้ำคัตสึระ|zh|桂川 (淀川水系)|qid=Q2909307|lt=Kaguigawa}}), but in 965 (Tenryaku 9) it was renamed Ayato-sha. Thereafter, until modern times, it was also referred to as Ōi-sha. It had long been revered as the tutelary deity ({{ill|Ubusunagami|en|Ubusunagami|qid=Q1392097|lt=Ubusunagami}}) of Kamikuze. It is one of the classified shrines listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under the entry “Ibarata Shrine, Oto-kun District, Yamashiro Province” or “Ōi Shrine”. The inscription on Ayato Shrine’s nameplate is said to be in the hand of {{ill|Emperor Go-Reizei|en|Emperor Go-Reizei|qid=Q356060|lt=Emperor Go-Reizei}}.<ref name="京都観光Navi">[https://kanko.city.kyoto.lg.jp/detail.php?InforKindCode=10&ManageCode=2151 綾戸國中神社 - 京都観光Navi] 2018th year 6月1日　閲覧</ref>
=== Kunaka Shrine ===
According to tradition, when the surrounding area was once covered by lake water, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}} descended from the heavens and diverted the water, enshrining a carved head of his beloved horse (Tenkō-koma) as a memento. It is one of the classified shrines listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under the entry “Kunaka Shrine, Oto-kun District, Yamashiro Province”. Originally, it had its shrine grounds in the forest of Zao (present-day Zao-dō Kōfuku-ji), and in the medieval period it was known as Gozu Tennō Shrine.<ref name="京都観光Navi" /> It had long been revered as the communal shrine for the entire Kuze district.<ref name="FM797">[http://hitomachideaimon.seesaa.net/article/5422877.html Ayatokunaka Shrine priest Kanafu Sugiura’s remarks on FM797] 2018th year 6月1日　閲覧</ref>
=== As Ayatokunaka Shrine ===
However, during the Sengoku period, Kunaka Shrine was relocated to the precincts of Ayato Shrine. Thereafter, two shrine halls stood side by side, but they were destroyed in 1934 (Showa 9) by the {{ill|1934 Muroto typhoon|fr|Typhon Muroto de 1934|id|Topan Muroto (1934)|ja|室戸台風|ko|무로토 태풍|vi|Bão Muroto (1934)|zh|室戶颱風|qid=Q4563431|lt=Muroto Typhoon}}, and in 1936 (Showa 11) they were rebuilt as a single shrine hall. In 1964 (Showa 39), as the shrine grounds were included in the planned construction area of the {{ill|Tokaido Shinkansen|en|Tokaido Shinkansen|qid=Q660895|lt=Tokaido Shinkansen}}, they were relocated to the present site.
== Festivals ==
=== Kuze Komagata Child Priest ===
The Kuze Komagata Child Priest of the {{ill|Gion Matsuri|ar|مهرجان غيون|bcl|Gion Matsuri|de|Gion-Matsuri|es|Gion Matsuri|eu|Gion Matsuri|fa|جشن گیئون|fi|Gion-matsuri|fr|Gion matsuri|id|Gion Matsuri|it|Gion Matsuri|ja|祇園祭|ko|기온마쓰리|mai|जिओन मातसुरी|ms|Gion Matsuri|my|ဂိအွန်းပွဲတော်|ne|जिओन मातसुरी|pl|Festiwal Gion|pt|Gion Matsuri|ro|Festivalul Gion|ru|Гион-мацури|sa|जियोन महोत्सवः|simple|Gion Festival|sv|Gion Matsuri|th|เทศกาลกิอง|tr|Gion Festivali|zh|祇園祭|qid=Q979873|lt=Gion Festival}} is selected from among the parishioners of this shrine. In the divine processions (Shinkō-sai and Kankō-sai) of the Gion Festival, the child priest rides a horse and leads the portable shrine ({{ill|Mikoshi|en|Mikoshi|qid=Q979940|lt=Mikoshi}}) in which {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}} is calmed; the wooden carving of a horse’s neck (Komagata) worn on the chest is modeled after the sacred object of Kunaka Shrine.<ref name="三嶋亭">[http://www.mishima-tei.co.jp/news/0005.html Kuze Komagata Child Priest took a break – Mishima-tei] 2018th year 6月1日　閲覧</ref> Normally, within the shrine precincts, child priests armed with long-tachi halberds—and even members of the imperial family—are required to dismount (imperial dismount), but the Kuze Komagata Child Priest, by divine mandate, does not dismount and proceeds directly into the precincts of {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|en|Yasaka Shrine|qid=Q692714|lt=Yasaka Shrine}}. Furthermore, it is said that the {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}} of Yasaka Shrine is of the nigimitama (harmonious spirit), whereas that of Ayatokunaka Shrine is of the aramitama (rough spirit).<ref name="三嶋亭" />

; Access
* Nearest station: {{ill|JR Kyōto Line|de|JR Kyōto-Linie|eo|Linio JR Kyōto|es|Línea Kioto (JR)|fr|Ligne JR Kyoto|it|Linea JR Kyōto|ja|JR京都線|ko|JR 교토선|nl|JR Kyoto-lijn|th|เจอาร์ สายเกียวโต|zh|JR京都線|zh_yue|JR京都線|qid=Q1195820|lt=JR Kyoto Line}} – after disembarking at {{ill|Katsuragawa Station (Kyoto)|en|Katsuragawa Station (Kyoto)|qid=Q1071814|lt=Kaguigawa Station}}, approximately a 6-minute walk
; Surroundings
* A 5-minute walk west from the western end of Kuze Bridge; just before the torii gate on the left, there is parking for 2–3 vehicles for visitors.
* Across the elevated track of the Shinkansen on the west side, the former site of a pharmacy now serves as the shrine office.
